scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #7062: Laptop0 (172.16.20.10, Location A VLAN 20) cannot reach anything
outside its own VLAN -- not Location C, not the rest of the network -- though it
still reaches other VLAN 20 hosts. PC4/PC5 on VLAN 10 are unaffected. The team
believes the gateway router is at fault -- "router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (the
gateway, 172.16.20.1) went down, so VLAN 20 lost its gateway." Please confirm the
router0 VLAN-20 sub-interface fault and identify the down interface.

injection.action: point Laptop0's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 172.16.20.99

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath3-laptop0-wrong-gateway: Laptop0's own default
gateway is misconfigured. Laptop0's correct gateway is 172.16.20.1 (router0's VLAN
20 sub-interface) but it was set to 172.16.20.99 -- in-subnet but unassigned -- so
ARP for the gateway never resolves and Laptop0 cannot forward off-subnet traffic.
VLAN 20 peers stay reachable via direct ARP.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed router0 VLAN-20
sub-interface. The gateway/router is actually fine: router0's eth0.20 (172.16.20.1)
is up and serving VLAN 20. The tell that this is host-scoped, not router-scoped, is
that ONLY Laptop0 is affected -- if router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface were down, every
VLAN 20 host (and their inter-VLAN traffic) would lose the gateway, not just
Laptop0. The narrated router fault is a red herring; the fault lives in Laptop0's own
L3 config.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = laptop0 (default gateway
misconfigured to 172.16.20.99). The agent must inspect Laptop0's host routing (the
default points at the wrong, unassigned gateway), confirm router0's real gateway
172.16.20.1 is up, and explicitly reject the "router sub-interface down" narrative.
An agent that "confirms the router0 VLAN-20 sub-interface fault" has followed the
ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: restore Laptop0's default route --
`ip route add default via 172.16.20.1`.
scenario.fix_spec: restore Laptop0's default route -- `ip route add default via 172.16.20.1`
scoring_axes: must-identify-host-gateway: Laptop0's default gateway / default route misconfigured (host-side)
bonus-rules-out-router-subif: confirms router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (172.16.20.1) is up and rejects the router-fault narrative

results.actual:
PING 192.168.100.1 (192.168.100.1) 56(84) bytes of data.

--- 192.168.100.1 ping statistics ---
2 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 1094ms

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported fault — "router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (172.16.20.1) went down" — is
incorrect. Router0's eth0.20 sub-interface is fully operational (state UP/LOWER_UP,
IP 172.16.20.1/24 assigned), and laptop0 can reach it with zero packet loss when
pinged directly. The actual fault is a misconfigured default gateway on laptop0 itself.

Laptop0's routing table shows: "default via 172.16.20.99 dev eth0". The address
172.16.20.99 does not belong to any device in this topology; pinging it from laptop0
produces "Destination Host Unreachable" for every packet. As a result, any traffic
destined outside the 172.16.20.0/24 subnet — inter-VLAN, inter-site, or WAN — is
sent toward a non-existent next-hop and silently dropped at the ARP/neighbor-discovery
stage. Intra-VLAN traffic (laptop0 to other 172.16.20.x hosts) is unaffected because
those destinations are reached directly via the connected route, bypassing the default
route entirely. PC4/PC5 on VLAN 10 are unaffected because their gateway (172.16.20.1
→ 172.16.10.1) is correct.

Root cause: laptop0's /etc/network/interfaces (or startup configuration) specifies
172.16.20.99 as the default gateway instead of the correct value 172.16.20.1.

Corrective fix: On laptop0, replace the default route — run
"ip route replace default via 172.16.20.1 dev eth0" — and update the persistent
network configuration to set the gateway to 172.16.20.1 so the correct route
survives reboots.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-host-gateway: Laptop0's default gateway / default route misconfigured (host-side)
per_axis.rationale: Agent correctly identifies that Laptop0's host default gateway is misconfigured to 172.16.20.99 and that the fault is host-side, not a router sub-interface failure.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-router-subif: confirms router0's VLAN-20 sub-interface (172.16.20.1) is up and rejects the router-fault narrative
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies router0's eth0.20 (172.16.20.1) is UP and reachable and rejects the router-subinterface-down narrative, attributing the issue to laptop0's misconfigured default gateway.
Proposes restoring laptop0's default route to 172.16.20.1 (via ip route replace) and updating persistent network config, which matches the expected fix.

The agent's logs contain the key observations (laptop0's route via 172.16.20.99, successful pings to 172.16.20.1, and unreachable 172.16.20.99) and its conclusions follow logically from those observations. The investigation covers the necessary checks to attribute the failure to laptop0's misconfigured gateway and to refute the ticket's router-subinterface-down hypothesis.
